# Automata Framework

> Automata is a deterministic 2D game framework for the web. A game builds for any static web host, for itch.io or for Ruken (automata-ship publishes to the last two), and a desktop build (Tauri) for Windows, macOS and Linux is planned.

## Documentation
- [Overview & Vision](/docs/overview): AI-assisted game development with code and content you can own.
- [Quick Start](/docs/quick-start): Play a double-jump remix, copy a task, and run the starter on your machine.
- [From Unity](/docs/from-unity): Map GameObjects, MonoBehaviours, scenes and ScriptableObjects to Automata ownership.
- [From Godot](/docs/from-godot): Map nodes, scenes, signals, resources and physics callbacks to simulation and presentation.
- [From Unreal](/docs/from-unreal): Map Actors, components, Blueprints and replication expectations to the current 2D framework.
- [From GameMaker](/docs/from-gamemaker): Map objects, instances, events, rooms and alarms to data, systems and content.
- [From web development](/docs/from-web): Map application state, components, requestAnimationFrame and async work to game ownership.
- [ECS Simulation & Determinism](/docs/sim-ecs): Components, systems, async creation and synchronous stepping.
- [PixiJS 2D Presentation](/docs/render-pixi): Renderer setup, render deltas and interpolation.
- [Effect Runtime & Concurrency](/docs/effect-runtime): Loading, errors and resource lifetimes outside the sim.
- [Zero-Eval CSP & Host Security](/docs/security-csp): Avoiding dynamic evaluation under the host policy.
- [Mobile UI Primitives](/docs/mobile-ui): Geometry, controls and accessible layout.
- [AI Coding Agent Rules](/docs/ai-rules): Project context for agents, followed by verification.
- [Capabilities and licensing](/docs/capabilities): What you can use today, what is planned, and how the license applies.
- [Boot errors](/docs/boot-errors): The typed failures boot reports, generated from the framework API index.
- [Install agent skills](/docs/agent-setup): Install Superpowers and the official PixiJS collection, then verify the agent can load them.
- [Who Automata is for](/docs/audience): Choose Automata based on your workflow and current requirements.
- [FAQ](/docs/faq): Answers about agents, content, licensing, platforms, migration and community games.

## AI & Agent Skills
- [Automata AI Portal](/ai): Project context, architectural rules, and verification guidance.
- [Full documentation](/llms-full.txt): The framework's defined documentation corpus and its complete API reference for version 0.0.3, generated from the package declarations.
- [API reference](/llms-api.txt): Every export of the 0.0.3 packages with its signature and doc comment, generated from the package declarations.
- [Site guides](/llms-guides.txt): The guides, task prompts and selected API examples on this site.

## API Reference
- [Simulation](/cheatsheet#simulation): Define gameplay state and advance it with synchronous fixed ticks. Use instance methods on the Sim returned by createSim.
- [Snapshots and replays](/cheatsheet#replays): Record accepted commands with checkpoints, encode a run, and verify it against matching plugins and content. Import replays through this simulation subpath.
- [Runtime](/cheatsheet#runtime): Effect-scoped boot, screens, loading, settings, and shutdown. Runtime service tags are available inside runtime-provided contexts.
- [PixiJS presentation](/cheatsheet#presentation): Draw render deltas without changing gameplay state. WebGL2 is the default; WebGPU is opt-in. Import no-eval before initializing PixiJS.
- [Responsive UI](/cheatsheet#ui): One geometry owner coordinates usable space, safe areas, browser bars, keyboard occlusion, and host display metrics. Svelte primitives consume that geometry.
- [Hosting](/cheatsheet#hosting): Use Hosting for readiness, capabilities, saves, lifecycle, and platform actions: one interface, whatever the game's target.
- [Content](/cheatsheet#content): Register Zod schemas for authored TOML, compile content, and pass the appropriate partition to the runtime or simulation.
- [Shipping](/cheatsheet#shipping): Configure identity and prepare a built folder. Preparation checks the local artifact; publishing needs a destination and credentials.
